title: Hamzated Verbs I — Initial Hamza
source: Original instructional lesson authored for this application (syllabus ref: Haywood & Nahmad Ch. 25; Ryding Ch. 2 §2.3.2, Ch. 22 §22.4)
objectives: Conjugate verbs with hamza as the first radical (e.g., أَخَذَ, أَكَلَ, أَمَرَ).
Apply the maddah spelling rule (آ) when hamza + fatḥah is followed by a vowelless hamza.
Form the irregular contracted imperatives خُذْ, كُلْ, and مُرْ.
recallPrompt: From Chapter 1: What sound does maddah (آ) represent?

sections.heading: Initial Hamza & Maddah Contraction
sections.body: Hamza (ء) is a full consonant, not a weak vowel. However, two hamzas in the same syllable cannot stand together: when 1st-person singular imperfect أَ + initial radical ءْ meet (e.g., أَأْخُذُ), they merge into maddah: آخُذُ ('I take').

sections.label: Irregular Initial-Hamza Imperatives
sections.summary: Three high-frequency initial-hamza verbs drop both the prosthetic hamzat al-waṣl and the initial radical hamza in the imperative: أَخَذَ → خُذْ ('take!'), أَكَلَ → كُلْ ('eat!'), أَمَرَ → مُرْ ('command!').

sections.irab: خُذِ: فِعْلُ أَمْرٍ مَبْنِيٌّ عَلَى السُّكُونِ | الكِتَابَ: مَفْعُولٌ بِهِ مَنْصُوبٌ
sections.notes: Notice the helping kasrah on خُذِ before hamzat al-waṣl in الكِتَابَ.

sections.heading: Form III & IV with Initial Hamza
sections.body: In Form IV past tense (أَ + أْمَنَ → آمَنَ 'he believed'), the two hamzas also merge into maddah (آ), while the imperfect is يُؤْمِنُ (hamza on wāw after ḍammah).
